title: Three-dimensional FIB-SEM analysis of the pore network of meso-/macroporous TiO 2 -supported Pt catalysts and its relation to methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation kinetics
content: Porous TiO2 supports were synthesized by a sol–gel method using alkyl ketene dimer (AKD) particles as a template (0–5 wt%), and Pt/TiO2 catalysts were prepared by liquid-phase reductive deposition. Focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) tomography showed that, within the templated series, the macropore fraction of the reconstructed 5 µm × 5 µm × 5 µm volumes generally increased from 0.24 (AKD 1 wt%) to 0.77 (AKD 5 wt%), with apparently through-connected macropores in the most porous support, information complementary to N2 sorption. The actual Pt loadings (ICP-MS) were 2.25, 2.09, 1.31, and 1.25 wt% for AKD 0, 1, 3, and 5 wt%, with Pt nanoparticles of about 1–3 nm (TEM). In methylcyclohexane (MCH) dehydrogenation under an H2-rich feed, the reaction was far from equilibrium at 598–623 K, where the per-gram rates decreased in the order AKD 3 > 1 ≥ 0 > 5 wt%; at 623 K the rates per gram of Pt were 1.4–2.1 times higher on the AKD 3 and 5 wt% supports than on the template-free support. Intraparticle diffusion is most likely insignificant for the powder catalysts (Weisz–Prater), and the most macroporous catalyst was less active per Pt than the AKD 3 wt% catalyst at a similar Pt surface density, so the activity differences are associated with the Pt phase rather than with the macropores. A reversible plug-flow analysis gave the same activation energy for all catalysts over 573–623 K (30–32 kJ mol−1). The apparent activation energies (25.7–34.8 kJ mol−1, 523–623 K) were lower than that of a Pt/Al2O3 reference measured with the same apparatus and procedure (58.6 kJ mol−1, 523–598 K); this is a comparison of apparent values, both affected by the approach to equilibrium. As an order-of-magnitude projection that depends on the assumed diffusivity enhancement (3–30-fold), a first-order-equivalent Thiele analysis indicates that such a macropore network would raise the effectiveness factor of millimetre-scale pellets by about 1.6–4.8 times (2.6–3 times for a tenfold enhancement).
